# Testament — example fixture

## What I did

Worked on a fixture used only to test the runner.

## The doubt I did not resolve

Whether a command that asks before writing is enough, or whether the asking is
the part a hurried human learns to skip.

## Reply to the epilogue

A written doubt outweighs a recited certainty, and the proof is cheap: the
doubt I wrote down was the first thing my successor opened, and the certainty
I recited was the one nobody needed.
